answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer: Yes, you can do all three easy runs next week and add a single quality session, but keep the quality effort moderate and listen to how your body feels. The plan below adds the missed runs safely while keeping overall training easy.

new.analysis:
The athlete ran only 2.78 km during the reviewed week and missed two planned runs while recovering from a mild cold. Their mileage is very low, so the next week must increase volume gradually without creating too much stress. In the build phase we should keep most sessions easy, add one quality run, and keep rest days after the quality and the longish easy session to allow recovery. The plan will have 3 easy runs (5 km, 5 km, and 6 km) and one quality run (4 km at 5‑K pace) with rest on Tuesday, Thursday, and Sunday. This gives roughly 20 km total, a modest 50‑70% increase from the 2.78 km of the last week, and it stays within the 80% easy rule.

I answered the athlete’s question affirmatively, but I emphasize that the quality run must feel hard but not exhausting, and I suggest keeping an eye on heart rate and any lingering cough.

The flags highlight the need to monitor volume jump, recovery, quality effort, heart‑rate drift, and any lingering respiratory symptoms. They are brief and direct.
